requirements.description: The system must allow an authenticated user to create a TODO. The create flow captures title, description, priority and due date, with optional assignment to a user, and then saves the TODO.
Each TODO must contain title, description, status, priority and due date. Optional notes can also be added (in scope). A title is mandatory.
Users must be able to edit TODOs they own or are authorized to manage. Editable information includes details, status, priority and due date, and reassignment where authorized.
Users must be able to mark TODOs as completed. A completed TODO must have Completed status.
Users must be able to assign a TODO to another authorized user, at creation (optional) or by reassignment where authorized. Team Leads can create and assign TODOs.
The system must support exactly the statuses Open, In Progress and Completed for TODOs.
The system must support the priorities Low, Medium, High and Critical for TODOs.
Users must be able to filter TODOs by status, priority, assignee and due date.
Users should be able to search TODOs by title or description.

The dashboard must show Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue TODO counts. The dashboard section also lists High/Critical priority TODOs. Overdue means the due date has passed and status is not Completed.
Team Leads must be able to view TODOs assigned to their team members (basic team view). This supports monitoring overdue work.
The system must maintain created-by, created-date, updated-by and updated-date for TODOs.
Users should be able to delete TODOs where permitted. Deleting a TODO must not delete the user account or other TODOs.
The system must prevent unauthorized modification of another user's TODO. Only authorized users can assign or modify TODOs.
The system must provide a web interface through supported browsers. The first release is web-based only, and there are no native mobile apps.

business_rules.text: A TODO must have a title.
A due date cannot be earlier than the creation date unless explicitly permitted.
Completed TODOs must have Completed status.
Only authorized users can assign or modify TODOs.
Overdue means the due date has passed and the status is not Completed.
Deleting a TODO must not delete the user account or other TODOs.

workflows.name: Create TODO
steps: Authenticated user opens the create TODO form

acceptance_criteria.given: An authenticated user is on the create TODO form
acceptance_criteria.when: They enter a title, description, priority and due date and save
acceptance_criteria.then: A TODO is created containing title, description, status, priority and due date

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is creating a TODO
acceptance_criteria.when: They try to save without a title
acceptance_criteria.then: The system does not save the TODO because a title is required

acceptance_criteria.given: A user owns a TODO or is authorized to manage it
acceptance_criteria.when: They edit its information and save

acceptance_criteria.given: A user can manage an Open or In Progress TODO
A user is authorized to assign TODOs
acceptance_criteria.when: They assign a TODO to another authorized user
acceptance_criteria.then: The TODO shows that user as assignee

acceptance_criteria.given: A user creates or edits a TODO
acceptance_criteria.then: The options available are Open, In Progress and Completed

acceptance_criteria.given: A user creates or edits a TODO
acceptance_criteria.then: The options available are Low, Medium, High and Critical

acceptance_criteria.given: Several TODOs exist with differing status, priority, assignee and due date
acceptance_criteria.when: A user applies a filter on any of these fields
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the matching TODOs are returned

acceptance_criteria.given: TODOs exist in various states, including some past their due date and not Completed
acceptance_criteria.then: Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue counts correctly reflect the TODO state

acceptance_criteria.given: A Team Lead has team members with assigned TODOs
acceptance_criteria.when: The Team Lead opens the team view
acceptance_criteria.then: The TODOs assigned to their team members are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: A TODO is created and later updated by different users
acceptance_criteria.then: Created-by, created-date, updated-by and updated-date reflect the actions performed

acceptance_criteria.given: A TODO belongs to another user and the current user is not authorized to manage it
acceptance_criteria.when: The user attempts to modify, assign or delete it

acceptance_criteria.given: A user has a supported browser
acceptance_criteria.then: The web interface is available and the core TODO functions can be used

acceptance_criteria.given: TODOs exist with various titles and descriptions
acceptance_criteria.when: A user searches for a term
acceptance_criteria.then: TODOs whose title or description match are returned

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is permitted to delete a TODO
acceptance_criteria.then: The TODO is removed, and the user account and other TODOs are unaffected

open_questions.question: What does 'authorized to manage' mean for each role (Employee, Team Lead, Administrator)? Who may edit, assign, reassign or delete which TODOs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: BR-003, BR-005, BR-013 and BR-014 depend on an authorization model that the BRD does not define.

open_questions.question: Who counts as an 'authorized user' to be assigned a TODO? Can an Employee assign TODOs to others, or only Team Leads?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The roles table gives assignment only to Team Leads, while BR-005 says 'users'.

open_questions.question: When may a due date earlier than the creation date be 'explicitly permitted', and who grants that permission?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The business rule has an undefined exception that affects validation.

open_questions.question: Is a High/Critical priority count a required dashboard item? BR-010 lists four counts, but section 7.3 adds High/Critical priority TODOs.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The dashboard scope differs between BR-010 and section 7.3.

open_questions.question: Should deletion be hard or soft, and should it be recoverable? Is a TODO's history retained for audit?
open_questions.why_it_matters: BR-013 and BR-012 do not specify delete behaviour or audit retention.

open_questions.question: What are the supported browsers and the agreed NFRs (performance, security, availability)? How do users authenticate (for example SSO)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: BR-015 and the acceptance criterion 'meets agreed NFRs' cannot be verified without them. The BRD also does not give a login method.

open_questions.question: How is team membership defined and maintained, for example whether a user can belong to several teams, and what scope a TODO's 'team' has?
open_questions.why_it_matters: BR-011 depends on the team structure, which XATA is to supply but which is not specified.

open_questions.question: Should Completed status be reversible, and how are status changes handled (for example reopening a completed TODO)? Is a TODO without an assignee allowed, and to whom does it belong?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The status workflow and the unassigned case are not specified.

open_questions.question: What are the Administrator's 'basic platform configuration' and user-management functions? There is no matching business requirement.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The role is described, but no BR covers user management or configuration. The scope also lists a 'basic user profile' without detail.

open_questions.question: The final acceptance criterion says the core lifecycle must be completed without administrator assistance. Which actions count as the core lifecycle?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The testable scope of this criterion is ambiguous.

assumptions.text: XATA will provide the user list and team structure.
XBS will propose the technical architecture based on the BRD and NFR.
The first release will use a single enterprise environment.
